posts.title: Chiplet Co-Design Framework Reduces Energy and Design Costs for AI Accelerators (University of Michigan)
posts.summary:
Researchers at the University of Michigan published a technical paper titled “Fengshui: Demystifying Chiplet Ecosystem and Bespoke Neural Network Accelerator Codesign.” Abstract Excerpt: “This paper introduces Fengshui, a chiplet ecosystem and accelerator co-design framework that jointly optimizes chiplet pool composition and bespoke application-specific integrated circuit (BASIC) design.” Find the technical paper here. September 2026. Jin,... » read more
The post Chiplet Co-Design Framework Reduces Energy and Design Costs for AI Accelerators (University of Michigan) appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: The University of Michigan's 'Fengshui' framework enables joint optimization of chiplet pool composition and bespoke ASIC design for AI accelerators.
The co-design approach targets reductions in both energy consumption and overall design costs by aligning hardware architecture with specific neural network requirements.
This framework addresses the growing need for efficient chiplet ecosystem management as AI hardware demands increasingly specialized, modular designs.

The post Agentic AI Automates Design-Rule Repair While Preserving Layout Equivalence (Purdue University) appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: The DRC-Aid framework automates local design-rule correction by utilizing inference-time large language models in a closed-loop verification process.
To manage the complexity of geometric repairs, the system employs a deterministic rule engine that translates physical verification violations into a constrained set of valid edits.
This approach aims to reduce manual intervention in physical design by automating the repair process while maintaining strict layout equivalence.

posts.title: How Robotics And Intelligent Equipment Control Drive Next-Gen Fab Productivity
posts.summary:
Behind the scenes, advanced equipment control and robotics are enabling higher levels of repeatability, tool uptime, and yield. 
The post How Robotics And Intelligent Equipment Control Drive Next-Gen Fab Productivity appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: Fabs are increasingly deploying collaborative robots and autonomous vehicles to replace manual tasks, aiming to boost operational uptime and ensure process repeatability.
Advanced equipment-control systems now integrate material, equipment, and wafer data to identify subtle variations before they impact yield, a critical capability for nanometer-scale manufacturing.

Rising capital costs—with gigascale fabs now reaching $20 billion—and global labor shortages are the primary drivers accelerating the adoption of AI-driven automation and fleet-management technologies.

posts.title: Mazda launches updated EZ-60 in China, adds LiDAR variants to close smart driving gap
posts.summary:
Changan Mazda rolled out the updated model a year after the EZ-60's launch, with limited-time prices starting at 113,900 yuan ($16,880).
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: Changan Mazda has updated the EZ-60 SUV to include four new LiDAR-equipped variants, signaling a strategic move to close the gap in advanced driver assistance systems (ADAS) within the competitive Chinese market.
The new LiDAR variants integrate Hesai's ATX sensor, which provides a 200-meter detection range and supports end-to-end architecture for both highway and urban navigation assistance.
Pricing for the updated lineup ranges from 113,900 yuan to 172,900 yuan, with the LiDAR-enabled versions commanding a 12,000 yuan premium over standard models.
Despite the addition of sophisticated sensing hardware, the vehicle's core dimensions and powertrain specifications remain largely consistent with the first-generation model launched in 2025.
